what: theodb_columnar GROUP BY pushdown. The M100 CustomScan admitted only a scalar aggregate and emitted one row; this slice admits a groupClause (bare-column keys of build_arrow-supported types incl. temporal, count(*)/sum(float8), no simultaneous WHERE), runs DataFusion .aggregate(group_exprs, agg_exprs), converts group keys back to PG datums (arrow_value_to_datum, reverse of build_arrow, in es_query_cxt for text-key lifetime), maps the output to PG target order via an explicit layout (agg-before-key correct), and emits N rows via a cursor.
hardware: DigitalOcean c-8 (8 vCPU CPU-Optimized dedicated), PostgreSQL 17.10 + pgrx 0.19.0, shared_buffers=2GB, work_mem=256MB
reproduce: benchmarks/columnar_groupby_ab.py (SET theodb.enable_columnar_agg=on; full top-level grouped result set fetched from the columnar CustomScan and compared row-by-row to the heap; speedup = GUC on vs off on the same columnar table)
goal: byte-identical grouped result set (columnar CustomScan vs heap native) AND CustomScan engaged (EXPLAIN) AND a measured speedup
verdict: GOAL MET. Top-level GROUP BY over a columnar table runs through the vectorized CustomScan, byte-identical to the native plan, 4.5x-9.75x faster across int / multi-key / temporal / agg-before-key shapes. The columnar pillar now supports vectorized GROUP BY key, sum/count.
caveats: Consuming a columnar-aggregate OUTPUT VALUE inside an enclosing expression (subquery/join over the agg value, or aggregate ORDER BY on it) hits a PRE-EXISTING M100 limitation (the scalar path fails identically: SELECT s+1 FROM (SELECT sum(x) s FROM col) q). Root cause: the planner inlines the Aggref of a scanrelid=0 CustomScan across SubqueryScan removal, re-evaluating the synthetic tuple (cache lookup failed for attribute N of relation 0). Orthogonal to GROUP BY, not introduced here, tracked separately. The canonical top-level SELECT key, agg FROM t GROUP BY key [ORDER BY ...] works. Scope: count(*)/sum(float8), bare-column keys, no simultaneous WHERE; other shapes decline to the native plan.
measurement_regime: GUC-on (CustomScan) vs GUC-off (native aggregate over the same columnar table); warm (in shared_buffers).
